title: Audit list endpoint does not clamp an attacker-controlled ?limit= parameter, enabling a resource-exhaustion DoS vector
description: audit-assurance.controller.js:478-484 builds AuditAssurance.find(filter).sort(sort).skip(skip).limit(parseInt(limit)) — limit is parsed with parseInt() but never clamped to a maximum. A caller can request ?limit=999999 (or a very large number) and force the server to fetch, populate, and serialize the organization's entire audit collection in one request, repeatable at will.
preconditions: Valid authenticated session with access to at least one organization's audits
Organization with a large audit collection (10,000+ documents) for realistic impact
steps: Call GET /api/audits?limit=999999&page=1 as an authenticated user
Repeat the call concurrently from multiple sessions
Monitor server memory/CPU and response latency for other tenants' requests during the burst
expectedResult: Current known behavior: the request succeeds and returns the full collection with no server-side clamp, and repeated concurrent calls measurably degrade response times for other requests. This should be flagged as a resource-exhaustion risk requiring a hard server-side maximum (e.g. clamp to 100) independent of client input.
requirement: OWASP API Security Top 10 - API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption

title: Vendor client-vendors list endpoint bypasses the shared pagination clamp helper, allowing an unbounded result set
description: vendor-service's BaseRepository.findPaginated (BaseRepository.ts:69-99) correctly clamps limit to Math.min(100, requestedLimit), but ClientVendorRepository.findClientVendors (:315-357) implements its own custom $facet aggregation pipeline that does not call this shared helper and applies $skip/$limit directly from caller-supplied values with no clamp — the same service enforces the cap inconsistently depending on which repository method serves the request.
preconditions: Valid authenticated session with vendor-management access
Organization with a large client-vendors collection
steps: Call the client-vendors list endpoint with an oversized limit parameter (e.g. limit=100000)
Compare the number of documents returned against the 100-row cap enforced elsewhere in the same service via BaseRepository.findPaginated
expectedResult: Current known behavior: the client-vendors endpoint returns more than 100 rows when an oversized limit is supplied, inconsistent with the rest of the service. Flag as a gap requiring the $facet pipeline to apply the same clamp as BaseRepository.findPaginated.
requirement: OWASP API Security Top 10 - API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption

title: Unbounded workflow-history fetch combined with per-entry lookups amplifies the cost of a single request
description: Security-relevant framing of PERF-INT-002: getMappingWorkflowHistory (evidence-mapping.controller.js:1339-1350) has no limit/skip on the history fetch and performs one findById per returned entry. An attacker who can generate many workflow-history entries on a mapping they control (e.g. by repeatedly toggling a status they're permitted to change) can inflate the cost of every subsequent read of that mapping's history, i.e. a self-inflicted but externally triggerable amplification.
preconditions: A mapping the test user has permission to repeatedly modify
steps: As a permitted user, script 500 rapid status-change round-trips on a single mapping to generate 500 WorkflowEntry records
Call GET .../mappings/:id/workflow-history and measure request duration and query count
Compare against a mapping with a normal (under 20) history length
expectedResult: Document the duration/query-count scaling between the two cases. Flag if the amplified case measurably exceeds a reasonable response-time budget (e.g. >2s), confirming the endpoint needs a history cap plus batched user resolution as remediation.
requirement: OWASP API Security Top 10 - API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption
